scenarios.title: Phasing permanents phase in or out in the active player's untap step

setup.notes: Tolarian Drake is a 2/4 flyer with phasing, currently phased in.

decisions: The untap step begins; the phasing turn-based action happens with no choices to take.

variants.label: phases_out
variants.expected: Tolarian Drake phases out in A's untap step: it is treated as though it does not exist (A controls no creature).

variants.label: phases_in
variants.delta: Tolarian Drake is phased out at the start of the untap step, having phased out while A controlled it.
variants.expected: Tolarian Drake phases in in A's untap step: it is on the battlefield again as a 2/4 flyer.

operation.unclassifiable: not a board edit: phased-out status of a permanent is set by no operation

variants.label: opponents_untap
variants.delta: The active player is B, so it is B's untap step (Tolarian Drake is phased in and A's).
variants.expected: Tolarian Drake does not phase: it stays phased in and A controls a 2/4 flyer.

operation.unclassifiable: phase or turn: it is B's untap step instead of A's

scenarios.forge_notes: Variant phases_in needs a phased-out permanent in the starting state; Forge represents it as a permanent with phasedOut set.

detector.outcome: In a player's untap step the turn-based phasing action phases permanents in or out: the turn_action record holds phased events.
detector.near_miss: No near miss is declared: an untap record with no phased event is not tagged.

scenarios.title: It becomes night at the untap step if it was day and the previous active player cast no spells

setup.notes: It is day, so Fearful Villager (daybound) is on its front face, a 2/3. The previous turn was B's turn. B did not cast any spell during it; Grizzly Bears stayed in B's hand.

decisions: The untap step begins; the day/night check happens as a turn-based action with no choices to take.

variants.label: no_spell
variants.expected: It becomes night: Fearful Villager transforms into Fearsome Werewolf, a 4/3 with menace.

variants.label: one_spell
variants.delta: B had cast Grizzly Bears during its previous turn (it is on B's battlefield, not in hand).
variants.expected: It stays day: Fearful Villager remains a 2/3 on its front face.

operation.unclassifiable: history: the number of spells B cast during its previous turn

scenarios.forge_notes: The day/night state and B's cast count of the previous turn are starting history fixed by the notes, not setup fields.

detector.outcome: At the untap step the day/night check makes it night: the turn_action record holds a day_night_changed event with to night.
detector.near_miss: No near miss is declared: a check that changes nothing leaves no event.

scenarios.title: It becomes day at the untap step if it was night and the previous active player cast two or more spells

setup.notes: It is night, so Fearful Villager (daybound) is on its night face, the 4/3 Fearsome Werewolf. The previous turn was B's turn. B cast both Grizzly Bears during it.

decisions: The untap step begins; the day/night check happens as a turn-based action with no choices to take.

variants.label: two_spells
variants.expected: It becomes day: Fearful Villager transforms back to its front face, a 2/3 with menace.

variants.label: one_spell
variants.delta: B cast only one Grizzly Bears during its previous turn (the other is in B's hand, not on the battlefield).
variants.expected: It stays night: the permanent remains the 4/3 Fearsome Werewolf.

operation.unclassifiable: history: the number of spells B cast during its previous turn

scenarios.forge_notes: In the one_spell variant the second Grizzly Bears is in B's hand.

detector.outcome: At the untap step the day/night check makes it day: the turn_action record holds a day_night_changed event with to day.
detector.near_miss: No near miss is declared: a check that changes nothing leaves no event.

scenarios.title: The active player's permanents untap simultaneously except those an effect keeps from untapping

setup.notes: Claustrophobia: enchanted creature doesn't untap during its controller's untap step.

decisions: The untap step begins; the untap turn-based action happens with no choices to take.

variants.label: aura_on_runeclaw
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears untaps; Runeclaw Bear (enchanted) stays tapped; B's Island stays tapped because B is not the active player.

variants.label: aura_on_grizzly
variants.delta: Claustrophobia is attached to Grizzly Bears instead of Runeclaw Bear.
variants.expected: Runeclaw Bear untaps; Grizzly Bears (enchanted) stays tapped.

operation.unclassifiable: not a board edit: an Aura attached to a different permanent; no operation sets attachment

variants.label: opponents_untap
variants.delta: The active player is B, so it is B's untap step.
variants.expected: B's Island untaps; A's Grizzly Bears and Runeclaw Bear stay tapped.

operation.unclassifiable: phase or turn: it is B's untap step instead of A's

detector.outcome: In the active player's untap step their tapped permanents untap together: the turn_action record holds untapped events.
detector.near_miss: No near miss is declared: a permanent an effect keeps tapped leaves no event.

scenarios.title: No player receives priority during the untap step, so no spell can be cast

setup.notes: Mountain is untapped. A is asked whether Lightning Bolt targeting Grizzly Bears can be cast at this point.

decisions: A attempts to cast Lightning Bolt targeting B's Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain, at the point named by the variant.

variants.label: untap_step
variants.expected: Casting Lightning Bolt is not legal (can_play false): no one receives priority in the untap step.

variants.label: upkeep_step
variants.delta: The attempt happens in the upkeep step (setup.step upkeep), where A receives priority.
variants.expected: Casting Lightning Bolt is legal (can_play true) with Grizzly Bears as a legal target.

operation.unclassifiable: phase or turn: the attempt happens in the upkeep step instead of the untap step

scenarios.forge_notes: The untap step has no priority in Forge; a playability query there may need to be modeled as the first priority of the upkeep. The second half of 502.4 (triggers waiting) is shown by scenario 503.1a-1.

detector.none: The rule's outcome is that nothing is cast, activated or resolved in the untap step because no player receives priority. Neither gen-2 nor gen-3 writes a decision record there: gen-3 writes decision candidates at every priority stop (record-schema-delta, behaviour changes) and the untap step is none, gen-2's AI-hook decisions likewise come only at priority. No playability record or verdict bit shows it; verdict_bit timing false would instead tag sorcery-speed candidates at other priority stops, another rule's outcome.
